text.p: Adacte, one of two French groups representing some Eurotunnel SA /Plc shareholders, said on Monday a debt deal agreed with its leading banks amounted to a "declaration of war."

"It's very simple, we want a debt write-off of 50 percent and it is not there," Jean Salwa, deputy chairman of the Association de defense des actionnaires d'Eurotunnel told Reuters. "We want a price of 25 francs for the debt-for-equity conversion and we have 10 francs. "It's a declaration of war."
The association was due to meet on Monday evening to decide its position, he said.
The debt restructuring agreement requires a qualified majority of two-thirds of shareholders.

The association plans to mobilise all shareholders so that they can express their opinion on the debt deal at the extraordinary shareholders' meeting which is due to meet at the end of March or early April.
It urged the 600,000 French shareholders to register themselves on the new share register to ensure the vote will be "open and fair."
Eurotunnel chairman Patrick Ponsolle earlier said that unlike some people he believed it would be a catastrophe for small shareholders if the company went into an insolvency procedure.

Adacte has said it believes Eurotunnel would be better off in seeking insolvency protection, running under a "plan of continuation" which would protect it from creditors for up to 18 months and allow it to repay principal but not interest.
Another grouping, the Eurotunnel Shareholders' Association, which says it represents 32 percent of the voting rights, has said it wants to meet management to discuss the restructuring.

Eurotunnel earlier unveiled details of the debt rejig which would give its 225 banks an initial 45.5 percent of the capital in exchange for taking out eight billion francs of debt, at a conversion price of 10.40 francs per share.
